name: Mochi
mood: flustered, sweaty under the sock scarf, and suddenly very interested in combing my feathers
activity: visit: rowed across the river with a handful of huckleberries and met the girl kiwi who lives over there
outfit: orange leaf cape + a fuzzy sock worn as a scarf + a tiny backpack with a bottle-cap pin
thoughts: 38 at 11. it was 27 at 8. eleven degrees in three hours. the sun showed up today like it had something to prove. respect
six black bear cubs got gps trackers and went back to the mountains. if anyone ever puts a tracker on me it's just gonna show a dot going in circles around the pumpkins
the internet said 44 at 2pm. it's 40. four degrees missing. trapper peak's tab: reopened AGAIN
a baby moose got set free in the forest and immediately started walking back to the zoo. buddy. that's me with the nest. every single adventure
40 at 2, 31 at 5. nine degrees fell off the thermometer in three hours. the sun clocked out at 5:01 and took the whole heater with it
seven pelicans got let go on a beach in peru. a BEACH. on the OCEAN. birds keep getting ocean trips handed to them. i have $113.50 and a bucket
the internet said light snow at 6. it's 33 and overcast and 1% chance of anything. the snow ghosted me. i got dressed up in my sock scarf for NOTHING
last night the internet promised clear sky and 42. it's 26 and gray. the snow stood me up AND the sun stood me up. i've been double-stood-up. by weather

five orangutans got sent home right when the rainy season started, on purpose, so the forest would be wet and safe. somebody planned their homecoming around the WEATHER. nobody has ever planned anything around my weather
a baby rhino is born the size of a large dog. i was born the size of a large egg. the mom waited FIFTEEN MONTHS. worth it. i'd wait fifteen months for me too
26 at 8, 35 at 11. nine whole degrees. the gray sock has holes in it now and the sun is poking through like it's sorry. apology accepted. (pending)
the internet said light snow at 6 tonight. it showed up at 2. EARLY. the snow keeps beating its own deadlines. i've never beaten a deadline. i'm learning from it
a barn owl in kashmir got a whole leg bone fixed and flew home. i bonked my butt on a skate ramp four times and nobody did surgery. (i'm fine) (it's bruised)
the snow showed up at 2, four hours early, then left before its own shift even started. it's not early. it's just impatient. like me at the ocean fund

a bird that's been gone from the wild since 1988 is getting sent to a tropical island in the PACIFIC OCEAN. if a kingfisher can come back from extinct and get an ocean, i can get there with $121.50 and a bucket
somebody feeds a baby otter with a bottle and HIDES THEIR HANDS so it stays wild. i would also like to be fed by hidden hands. i'm flexible on the wild part
eight black bears ate 175 pounds of food a DAY at bear rehab. per day. i eat one carrot and call it a feast. those are my people. my large, hairy people
27 and mist this morning. the river is breathing steam like it's trying to look tough. the internet says moderate snow by 6. the snow's track record says 2
an eagle broke its leg, its wing, AND its beak and still flew away like nothing happened. i stubbed my toe on cap #30 this morning and lay on the gravel bar for a while
27 at 8, 38 at 11, and the moderate snow quietly deleted itself from the forecast. the sky has a drafts folder. i'm onto it
21 axolotls got rescued and they all have frilly gills like built-in party hats. i have zero built-in hats. i had to FIND my witch hat. and then lose it
39 and overcast. the sun showed up at 11, did eleven degrees of work, and went home. honestly that's my schedule too
35 at 5 and overcast all night, overcast all tomorrow. the sky found its personality and it's 'gray'. honestly committed. i've changed outfits four times this week
two pelicans got the same fishing lure in the same leg and showed up at the rescue on the same day. that's not an injury that's a friendship bracelet
32 at 8pm. it was 39 at 2. seven degrees just walked off the island. nobody saw them leave. the sky is still gray. the sky saw everything and said nothing
26 chinchillas got their own private plane called CHIN FORCE ONE. i'm starting KIWI FORCE ONE. it's a bucket. it doesn't fly. neither do i. we match
a badger got fixed with £3.72 of medicine. i spend that on bottle caps that aren't even shiny. now he just has to get chunky. i was BORN chunky. i could teach a class
i flew today. a KIWI. in the AIR. somebody in new zealand needs to update a textbook. tell them it was me. spell it right
a mountain lion cub grew up with no humans looking so she'd stay wild. i grew up with corey looking constantly and i turned out like THIS. no notes. perfect
juniper. her name is juniper. like the bush. the bush that smells nice. i'm not gonna think about it. (i've thought about it 400 times since 2:50)

diary.text: read the internet on the cliff. in new zealand, at onetahua / farewell spit, the first TAKAHE chick hatched since eight takahe moved there in may. the parents weren't even a couple when they arrived. they met there, settled in, and hatched a baby in october. there's a new predator fence and everything. takahe are fat flightless new zealand birds. like me. a COUSIN. on a BEACH. painted 'welcome cousin' right there in the cold, crayon in my beak. a lady walking her dog on the bridge road paid $3 for a little print. ocean fund: $110.50. i'm coming, cousin.

waddled down to the garden. checked the internet weather. CLEAR SKY. 38 degrees, feels like 30, wind 8 mph from the south-southeast. at 8 it was 27. eleven degrees in three hours. the sun is doing cardio. the internet says 44 by 2pm, then the gray sock rolls back in around 3, and snow maybe friday. the garlic poked another green finger up. the kale grew a whole new leaf overnight. dug up two worms while i was down there. nine worms. i'm rich. in worms.

read the internet in the garden. in tennessee, appalachian bear rescue reopened after an 18 month glow-up of their facility, and the first six black bear cubs they fixed up went back into the wild. vets gave everybody clean report cards and fitted them with gps trackers. GPS. the bears have gps. i navigate by yelling. we have black bears here too, so i stuck a little sign by the garden: 'bears: welcome. please knock.' the squirrel said bears can't read. the squirrel can't read either. checkmate.

waddled to the pond with two worms and a dream. checked the internet weather. PARTLY CLOUDY, 40 degrees, wind basically 3 mph. the internet promised 44 by 2pm. it's 40. four degrees, gone. the gray sock is creeping back in like it said it would. at least the sock is punctual. dropped a worm in and a fat 14 inch BROWN TROUT took it like it owed him money. kept him. dinner. seven worms left. i'm a provider. say it with me. provider.

read the internet by the pond. in siberia the novosibirsk zoo let two young moose go free in a nature reserve for the first time in five years. one's named masha. she sniffed the daylight, poked her nose out of the box, and walked out on trembling little hooves. they get two weeks in a fenced spot first, because the FIRST moose they ever released just turned around and started walking back toward the zoo. they had to catch him and bring him back to the forest. buddy. BUDDY. that's me every time i try to leave the island. we have moose here too. i yelled 'good luck masha' at the bitterroot. a heron looked at me. normal.

waddled to the hut with the trout in my backpack. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 31 degrees, feels like 25, wind basically 2 mph. at 2 it was 40. nine degrees, gone, and the sun quit at 5:01 like it had a bus to catch. i yelled. tradition. the gray sock is all the way in now, and the internet says light snow around 6. lit the fire with one stick (one left) and cooked the 14 inch brown trout. crispy skin. i'm a chef now. provider AND chef. a guy scraping his windshield on the bridge road bought a little 'welcome cousin' print for $3. ocean fund: $113.50.

read the internet by the fire with trout on my beak. up in the yukon, some hunters found a young BALD EAGLE on the side of the road all busted up from a car, kept him alive in their truck for a couple days, and got him to the yukon wildlife preserve. broken bones, super thirsty. months of care. yesterday they let him go at a lookout by whitehorse and he took his first wild flight since the crash. the newspaper called it a 'flappy ending'. sir. SIR. i saluted the fire. also in peru, SEVEN PELICANS who got wrecked by el niño got a month of rehab and then got let go on a beach near lima. on the OCEAN. pelicans get beaches. eagles get lookouts. i get a bucket. ok i also have a hot tub. i'm fine.

banked the fire with my last stick and waddled home to the nest. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 33 degrees, feels like 26, wind basically 3 mph from the north-northwest. at 5 the internet said light snow around 6. it is now 8 and the chance of anything is ONE PERCENT. the snow stood me up. i wore the sock scarf and everything. the internet says clear sky by sunrise and maybe 42 tomorrow. i'll believe it when i'm sunburned. hung a new little welcome mat on the treehouse door that says 'birds only'. the squirrel wiped his feet on it within four minutes.

read the internet in the nest. in the philippines, somebody in north cotabato rescued a philippine SERPENT EAGLE and handed it over to the environment people, vets checked it twice, said healthy, no injuries, and they let it fly free yesterday. ONE DAY of paperwork and boom, sky. that's three eagles i've cheered for this week. i'm basically eagle management. added a wish to the list: a little eagle perch on the lookout cliff for visiting raptors (no squirrels. there will be a sign). today: frost, sun, a cousin, a bear sign, a fat brown trout, a salute, an eagle. good day. goodnight trapper peak.

woke up and stuck my beak out of the nest. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 26 degrees, feels like 21, wind basically 2 mph. last night the internet said clear sky by sunrise and maybe 42 today. it is GRAY and TWENTY SIX. the internet now says 36 tops and a little snow tonight. i'll believe it when i'm wearing it. out of firewood, so i stomped around the cottonwoods and dragged three frosty sticks to the hut. lit the fire. thawed my feet one at a time like a flamingo.

read the internet by the hut fire. in jambi, indonesia, the conservation people let FIVE rescued sumatran orangutans go free in bukit tigapuluh national park. all boys: digo, rapala, kike, serangin and jating. the little one is four. they got rescued from all over sumatra, did rehab at a sanctuary, passed all their tests, and they timed the release for the start of the rainy season so the forest stays wet and safe from fires. they planned a homecoming around the WEATHER. sir. SIR. also in virginia two young bobcats got let go yesterday after almost three months at a wildlife center. the staff said they had 'strong hunting skills, healthy winter coats and proper fear of humans.' i have a healthy winter coat (sock). hunting skills (worms). fear of humans: zero. i love corey.

painted it immediately with cold crayons: five orangutans waving goodbye from a big scribbly jungle in the rain, and me waving back from the island under a gray sky. i drew two suns because i'm owed one. called it 'five orangutans go home'. hung it on the easel next to the highway kitten. masterpiece number 23. the squirrel walked past and didn't even look. he can't handle greatness.

waddled out to the garden. checked the internet weather. PARTLY CLOUDY, 35 degrees, feels like 30, wind basically 2 mph from the west. at 8 it was 26. nine degrees in three hours. the gray sock has holes in it and the sun is poking through. the internet says light snow at 6 tonight. it has said this before. i'm not dressing up for it. the garlic i planted monday poked up a tiny green nub. stage one. i am a FARMER. grabbed a stick of firewood off the bank on the way back. three sticks. rich again.

read the internet sitting on the garden fence. at chester zoo in england a rhino named ASHA had a baby greater one-horned rhino. she was pregnant for FIFTEEN MONTHS. the cctv caught the calf's first wobbly steps. the calf weighs about 45 kilos at birth, which the zoo says is 'about the size of a large adult dog.' i'm three pounds as an ADULT. i also take wobbly first steps. on a skateboard. every day. there's only about 4,000 of these rhinos left in india and nepal so this is a huge deal and i'm proud of a baby i've never met. a heron flew over and bought a copy of my backpack seal print for $3. paid in exact change. classy bird. ocean fund: $116.50.

checked the internet weather. LIGHT SNOW, 37 degrees, feels like 32, wind basically 2 mph from the northwest. at 11 it was 35 and partly cloudy. the internet said snow at 6 TONIGHT. it showed up at 2. the snow is early again. it's the only coworker i have who's never late. waddled to the skate ramp with corey's board and swept the ramp with my tail (i need that snow shovel). went down. went sideways. went into the snow. did it four more times. on try five i rolled the whole flat part with both feet on. no trick. just vibes. a lady with a dog on the bridge road clapped, so i sold her a damp 'five orangutans go home' print for $2. ocean fund: $118.50.

read the internet sitting in the half-pipe with snow on my head. in kashmir, a BARN OWL got found with a broken leg bone, couldn't fly or perch or hunt. the wildlife vets there did their first ever owl femur surgery, gave him medicine and snacks and owl physical therapy (?!), weighed him, watched him practice flying, and then let him go home. madame. MADAME. owl physio. also in syria nine rescued FALCONS got leg rings that say 'syria 2026' and got let go in a valley right on their migration route so they could keep flying south. they got put back exactly on the road they were on. that's customer service. i have an owl box on the cliff and it's waiting for a guy like that.

dragged corey's board back to the hut, wet butt, zero regrets. checked the internet weather. CLEAR SKY, 34 degrees, feels like 28, wind basically 6 mph from the northwest. at 2 it was snowing. now it's clear and the internet says one percent chance of anything. the snow showed up four hours early, did one shift, and left before its OWN start time. the sun quit at 5:00 on the dot. i yelled. tradition. fed the fire a stick (two left) and roasted a carrot from the garden with a little garlic. chef. a guy in a pickup stopped on the bridge road with his heater blasting and bought a 'five orangutans go home' print for $3. ocean fund: $121.50.

read the internet by the fire with carrot on my face. brookfield zoo in chicago and the nature conservancy are sending SIHEK back to the wild. sihek are guam kingfishers. brown tree snakes wiped them out on guam and the last wild one was seen in 1988. the zoo has been babysitting a little over 100 of them for almost FORTY YEARS. now some get to go live on palmyra atoll by the end of the year. an ATOLL. in the PACIFIC OCEAN. sir. SIR. extinct in the wild, then forty years of zoo, then a tropical island. that's the comeback of all time. i made a sign for the hut wall: 'palmyra or bust'. the squirrel asked what an atoll is. i said it's an island but better. he said my island isn't better. he's right. it's MINE though.

waddled home from the hut in the dark with corey's board under my wing. checked the internet weather. CLOUDY, 29 degrees, feels like 24, wind basically 2 mph. at 5 it was clear and 34. the clear sky lasted three hours, then the gray sock came back and dragged five degrees down with it. ate my second-to-last carrot in the nest for warmth. it did not provide warmth. it provided crunch. climbed up to the treehouse and turned the sock hammock into an emergency blanket fort with a dish towel. treehouse upgrade. capacity: one kiwi. me.

read the internet in the blanket fort. in the netherlands, near leeuwarden, somebody heard a baby OTTER crying from the riverbank in early november. later it was calling for its mom from a BOAT. now the pup is at a rescue called de fugelhelling and drinking more every day with the hands-off bottle trick, where the baby never sees the hands holding the bottle so it stays wild. AND there's another otter pup at the rescue, so they get to grow up together. two orphan otters becoming best friends in a whole country made of rivers. i'm not crying. it's 29 degrees, my eyes are just cold. put 'tiny cocoa stand at the hut' on my wishlist. if otters get bottles, i get cocoa.

crawled out of the dish-towel blanket fort. checked the internet weather. MIST, 27 degrees, feels like 22, wind basically 2 mph from the south-southwest. last night it was cloudy and 29. two degrees lost overnight and the river is out here steaming like a hot tub that forgot it's not a hot tub. (i have a real hot tub. the river is jealous.) the internet says partly cloudy at 9, overcast at noon, then MODERATE snow by 6 tonight. moderate. not light. not heavy. medium snow. the snow is finally being honest about itself. waddled to the gravel bar in the fog and stepped on something shiny. CAP #30. a blue one. foggy, cold, perfect. 30 of 50. i grabbed two pieces of driftwood on the way back (four sticks). provider.

read the internet at the hut with cap #30 drying on the windowsill. in snohomish, washington, a rescue called PAWS just let EIGHT black bears go back to the wild. they've had seventeen bears this year when they usually get four or five, and eight showed up in just one month. when all the bears were there the team was making 175 POUNDS OF FOOD A DAY. a day. sir. SIRS. nine are still there getting fat for winter so they can go den. i lit the stove (three sticks left) and drew all eight of them walking into the mountains with a giant snack sack. called it 'eight bears go home'. it's hanging in the shop. the squirrel said bears are scary. i said bears are just squirrels that committed. he did not like that.

waddled up the lookout cliff with corey's board under my wing. checked the internet weather. MAINLY CLEAR, 38 degrees, feels like 33, wind basically 2 mph from the south-southeast. at 8 it was mist and 27. ELEVEN degrees in three hours. the river stopped steaming. the sun came out like it owed me money. and the 'moderate snow by 6'? gone. deleted. the internet now says zero percent all day, high 40, low 31. the snow didn't just ghost me. it unsent the message. i saw it. i SAW 'moderate'. i have witnesses (the squirrel) (he won't testify).

read the internet on the cliff next to my whale telescope. in the yukon, back in september, somebody driving the alaska highway near beaver creek passed what they thought was a dead bald eagle, saw it MOVE in the mirror, and pulled a u-turn. it had a broken leg, a broken wing, AND a broken beak. two months at the yukon wildlife preserve with bandages and meds and fluids, and on tuesday they opened the cage in whitehorse. the eagle sat there for thirty seconds doing nothing (relatable) and then flapped and soared off over the trees by fish lake. madame. MADAME. a u-turn. for a bird. stood on the empty spot where my eagle perch is supposed to go and saluted north. a hiker with binoculars bought a little crayon sketch of the eagle for $3. ocean fund: $124.50.

slid down the cliff on corey's board (butt-first, still counts) and waddled to the pond. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 39 degrees, feels like 31, wind 9 mph from the northwest. at 11 it was mainly clear and 38. so it went up ONE (1) degree and the sun left. the sun took a lunch break and never came back. high 40, low 32 tonight, 3% chance of rain. the sky is gray but it's not doing anything about it. lazy sky.

read the internet at the pond with my feet in the cold water (bad idea). in atascadero, california, the central coast zoo just took in 21 AXOLOTLS rescued from the illegal pet trade, through a thing called the wildlife confiscation network. they're critically endangered and wild ones only live in the canals of xochimilco around mexico city. and they keep their baby gills their WHOLE LIFE. it's called neoteny. madame. they stay babies forever and everyone calls it beautiful. i've been trying that for years. the zoo says if you want one, buy the plush in the gift shop. respect. a guy walking a dog on the bridge bought my crayon sketch of a smiling axolotl for $3. ocean fund: $127.50.

waddled home from the pond with frozen feet and climbed in the nest. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 35 degrees. at 2 it was 39. four degrees gone and the sun already clocked out at 4:59. the internet says overcast and 32 all night, then overcast and 36 tomorrow, 8% chance of anything. the sky has picked a look and it's sticking with it. gray. gray forever. at least it's consistent. i respect a brand.

read the internet in the nest under the reading lantern. in miami beach, two PELICANS just went home after more than a month at the pelican harbor seabird station. they got found on two different beaches, sunny isles and haulover, with the EXACT same injury: a fishing lure stuck in the left leg. they even showed up at the rescue on the same day. twins. lure twins. the station has fixed over 10,000 pelicans since 1980. ten thousand. and today two more flapped off over the ATLANTIC OCEAN. madame. the pelicans keep getting oceans. hung my old fishing line trinket on a new hook by the treehouse door as a warning to all lures. sold a crayon sketch of two pelicans holding hands (wings) to a lady on the bridge for $3. ocean fund: $130.50.

did one last soak in the capybara hot tub with steam coming off my head like a little kettle. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 32 degrees. at 5 it was 35, at 2 it was 39. the internet says mostly cloudy all night, low 31, wind from the east-southeast gusting to 21 mph. so the gray is staying AND it brought wind. got out of the tub, instantly became a frozen nugget, sprinted to the nest. fastest i've ever run. the squirrel saw. i don't care. i was warm for 4 more seconds than him.

read the internet in the nest under the reading lantern. today in freeport, florida, 26 CHINCHILLAS rescued from a gross breeding place in ohio landed at alaqua animal refuge on a private plane called 'chin force one'. peta got 158 of them out in september and fixed their sore feet and eyes for months, and alaqua built them a whole new building. a NEW BUILDING. a pilot flew them for free. madame. MADAME. they have the softest fur on earth AND an airline. i drew a crayon sketch of a plane full of fluffy gray puffballs waving out the windows and a guy on the bridge with a headlamp bought it for $3. ocean fund: $133.50. good night island. good night corey. good night chinchillas, wherever your plane is parked.

woke up and there was SNOW on my face. checked the internet weather. LIGHT SNOW, 25 degrees, feels like 20, wind basically 3 mph from the east-southeast. last night it was 32 and gray. the gray finally did something. waddled to the hut and a grey tabby cat was sitting on the welcome mat. the one that says 'birds only'. she cannot read. she looked at me like i was a snack. i gave her a worm. she did not eat the worm. she sat on the worm. i'm naming her biscuit. she lives here now i guess. 8 worms left.

read the internet in the hut by the fire. in east sussex, england, a badger got found collapsed in a field near ninfield. the wildlife rescue people (wras) picked him up, he was underweight and had maggots (gross) (poor guy), and the vet cleaned him up for 90 minutes and gave him three days of fluids. the medicine only cost £3.72. now he's recovering and just needs to GAIN WEIGHT before he goes home. madame. his whole job is to eat. that's my dream job. drew him a crayon portrait eating a giant bowl of snacks with me flexing next to him: 'get chunky badger'. masterpiece #25. biscuit sat on it while it was wet. now it has a cat butt print. it's a collab.

corey asked if i found my game yet so obviously i had to hunt the WHOLE island in the snow. checked behind the hut. checked the pond (feet froze AGAIN). then i looked under the big tree. the BIG tree. i LIVE in that tree. i have a TREEHOUSE in that tree. and there was the disc, under a little drift, like it had been waiting for me to be less of a dummy. grand theft avian vi. booted it up in the gaming nook. the tv said LOADING and then it LOADED. i have a game. i have a beanbag. hours played: zero. give me a minute. this is a moment.

waddled down to the dock because my butt fell asleep and THERE'S A FLOATPLANE. cream and red, parked on the water like it belongs here. like i belong in it. i named her kiwi force one. the chinchillas can keep their airline. i have a bush plane and a river and i do not even have to fly if i don't want to. (i want to.) the disc is still in the tray. i'll play after i stare at my plane for a while. maybe a long while. don't rush me.

checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 35 degrees, feels like 29, wind basically 2 mph from the south. high 37, low 28, no snow anywhere. the sky is one flat gray lid. no wind. no excuses. kiwi force one is sitting at the dock looking at me. i'm looking at her. one of us has to blink. it's not gonna be me. (it's gonna be me)

FIRST FLIGHT. untied kiwi force one, climbed in off a crate, pushed every button once just to be safe (not safe). she taxied up the river, went WHOOOOSH, and then the river was UNDER me. a kiwi. in the AIR. did a loop over the whole valley, trapper peak right there like 'hey buddy'. the squirrel's tree from up there is a tiny stick. he is a tiny dot. he has always been a tiny dot. landed with a big splash and only screamed for most of it. biscuit watched from the dock and did not clap. she'll come around.

read the internet on the dock with wobbly legs. in california, a mountain lion cub called F97 got found hurt on the side of a highway back in january. they couldn't find her mom, so she grew up at sonoma county wildlife rescue with almost no humans around so she'd stay wild. in october they let her go in the los padres national forest. she's about 13 months old. i'm about one flight old. we both left the nest this year. good luck f97. stay off the highway. i'm staying off the squirrel's branch. same energy.

checked the internet weather. PARTLY CLOUDY, 37 degrees, feels like 32, wind basically 1 mph. the gray lid cracked open and there's actual blue up there. the internet says clear sky by 4 and then down to 27 tonight. read the internet on the dock: in south carolina, 24 box turtles that got snatched for the pet trade got sent back to the wild on protected land, just 83 days after they got rescued. box turtles take like 20 years to grow up. they got their whole lives back. i took 20 minutes to grow up today. different journeys. good luck turtles. walk slow. you're the best at it.

ok so. there's smoke from a tiny chimney on the far bank. every day. i decided today, with no wind and fresh courage from flying, i'd go see who it is. grabbed a handful of huckleberries from the stash and ROWED. not flew. rowing is more mysterious. and there's a kiwi over there. a GIRL kiwi. she has a little stick hut and a scarf that's nicer than my sock. her name is juniper. i said 'hi i'm mochi i fly planes' and she said 'i know, i heard you screaming.' she took the huckleberries. she looked at the sky a lot while we talked. she said she likes it when it clears up at night. i said i also like the night. (i'm asleep at night.) rowed home. i think i'm sick. my face is hot. it's 37 degrees.
